# HTTP Collector

Fetches an HTTP endpoint and evaluates the configured policies against the response, for health monitoring and
compliance validation.

This plugin is intended to be run as part of an agent to validate HTTP endpoints against defined compliance policies.

This page is for **operators** who run the `plugin-http-collector` plugin with the CCF Agent, and for **developers** who write policies for it. It documents [v0.2.2](https://github.com/compliance-framework/plugin-http-collector/releases/tag/v0.2.2) and is generated from the plugin's [README at v0.2.2](https://github.com/compliance-framework/plugin-http-collector/blob/v0.2.2/README.md).

## Configuration

The plugin supports the following configuration options:

- `url` (required): The HTTP endpoint URL to test
- `method`: HTTP method to use (default: "GET") 
- `timeout`: Request timeout in milliseconds (default: 5000)
- `basic_auth`: Enable basic authentication (default: false)
- `basic_auth_username`: Username for basic auth
- `basic_auth_password`: Password for basic auth
- `additional_headers`: Additional headers in format "Key1: Value1;Key2: Value2"
- `check_certificate`: Validate SSL certificates (default: true)
- `body_regex_pattern`: Regex pattern to match against response body

## Policy input

One run makes one request to the configured `url` and evaluates every policy package against the response, so a policy receives one document per run as `input`: the response, as JSON. When no response was received (the request could not be built or sent, or its body could not be read) the plugin still evaluates the policies, with `success` false and `error` set, so a policy can record the failure as evidence. Fields are listed by their name in the document. A field marked as left out is missing from the document, not null, so test for it with `object.get` or a default. Your own policy data from the agent configuration is in `data.<key>`, not in `input`.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `status_code` | integer | HTTP status code of the response. 0 when no response was received. |
| `status` | string | Status line as Go reports it, such as `200 OK`. Empty when no response was received. |
| `headers` | object (string to array of strings) | Response headers, with Go's canonical names (`Content-Type`) and the list of values for each. Can be `null` when no response was received. |
| `body` | string | Response body as text. Empty when no response was received. |
| `response_time_ms` | integer | Time the request took, in milliseconds. |
| `success` | boolean | True for a 2xx status, false for any other status and when no response was received. |
| `error` | string | Why no response was received. Left out when a response was received, whatever its status. |
| `matched_regex` | boolean | True when the body matches `body_regex_pattern`. Left out when the pattern is not configured, does not compile, or does not match. |
| `body_regex_pattern` | string | The configured `body_regex_pattern`. Left out when it is not configured or does not compile. |

An example input:

```json
{
  "status_code": 200,
  "status": "200 OK",
  "headers": {
    "Content-Type": [
      "application/json"
    ],
    "Content-Length": [
      "27"
    ]
  },
  "body": "{\"status\":\"ok\",\"version\":\"1\"}",
  "response_time_ms": 150,
  "success": true,
  "matched_regex": true,
  "body_regex_pattern": "\"status\":\"ok\""
}
```

## Subject templates

The subject templates this plugin registers. Each example is built from sample data.

### http-endpoint

One endpoint per URL and HTTP method, registered when the agent calls `Init` with protocol v2. Title: `HTTP Endpoint: {{ .method }} {{ .url }}`. Every evidence carries both identity keys as labels, next to the `provider` label (`http`), so the API links it to one subject per endpoint and method. Agents that don't call `Init` (protocol v1) get the same evidence.

| Identity key | Description |
|---|---|
| `url` | The URL requested, the `url` setting as written. |
| `method` | The HTTP method used, in upper case (`GET` unless `method` is set). |

Example:

```json
{
  "name": "http-endpoint",
  "type": "component",
  "title": "HTTP Endpoint: GET https://status.example.com/health",
  "description": "HTTP endpoint https://status.example.com/health checked with GET",
  "purpose": "Represents an HTTP endpoint whose availability and response are checked",
  "identityLabels": {
    "url": "https://status.example.com/health",
    "method": "GET"
  }
}
```

## Policies

The policy bundles that work with this plugin, at their newest releases. The controls are the ones the bundle's policies list in their metadata.

| Bundle | Latest version | Controls covered | Compatible plugin lines |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`plugin-http-collector-policies`](https://github.com/compliance-framework/plugin-http-collector-policies) | `v0.2.1` | *none listed* | latest |

The plugin evaluates the policy bundles listed under `policies` in the agent's plugin config, usually the
[plugin-http-collector-policies](https://github.com/compliance-framework/plugin-http-collector-policies) bundle:

```yaml
plugins:
  health-checker:
    source: ghcr.io/compliance-framework/plugin-http-collector:<version>
    policies:
      - ghcr.io/compliance-framework/plugin-http-collector-policies:<version>
    config:
      url: https://example.com/health
```

Each run makes one request and evaluates every policy package in every bundle against it, producing one evidence
per package. Without `policies` the plugin makes the request but produces no evidence.

Policies are Rego v1 and live under the `compliance_framework.http_collector` package. They report failures with
a `violation` set, and set `title`, `description` and optionally `labels` (merged into the evidence labels):

```rego
package compliance_framework.http_collector.ensure_success_status

import rego.v1

violation contains {} if {
	not input.success
}

title := "HTTP endpoint should return successful status codes"
description := "HTTP endpoints should return 2xx status codes to ensure proper service functionality"
labels := {"severity": "high"}
```

### Policy data

`policy_data` from the agent config is passed to the policies as `data`.

### Evidence

Each evidence carries:

- labels `provider: http`, `url` and `method` (with the policy's `_policy` and its own `labels`). Together with
  the policy they derive the evidence UUID, so the same endpoint and policy keep one evidence history across runs;
- props `http_url`, `http_method`, `status_code`, `response_time_ms` and `success`, plus `error` when the request
  failed and `regex_pattern` and `regex_matched` when `body_regex_pattern` is configured;
- the `HTTP Health Check` activity (client settings, request, response size and time), followed by the policy
  manager's activities;
- the endpoint URL as a component subject, and start and end times of the request.

The response itself (the policy input above) is recorded with the evidence's policy evaluation.
